transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I don’t want to sound difficult or paranoid or anything… I’m generally a reasonable person. But I’ve been having a problem in my apartment building for several months now.

It seems like the property manager, and maybe a few people in the building, have been… sort of pressuring me to leave. There’s been misdelivered mail, noises in the walls that happen at very specific times, and little comments from neighbors that line up too neatly to be coincidence. They give me paperwork or explanations, but honestly, the pattern is still there. I thought it might help to talk to someone about it, if that makes sense.
Do you believe for certain that the property manager and your neighbors are deliberately trying to force you out?

I mean… “for certain” is a strong way to put it, and I don’t want to sound unreasonable. But yes, I do believe it’s deliberate. It’s been going on for months — the mail being sent to the wrong place, the noises in the walls happening at these specific times, and then neighbors making little comments that seem to connect to it.

They’ve given me paperwork and explanations, and I’ve tried to consider those, really. But the pattern is still there. I can see it, and it feels very much like they’re trying to pressure me out of the apartment.
Have you heard voices when no one was actually there?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I hear noises sometimes, like I mentioned, but not voices talking to me when nobody’s there. At least… not that I’d describe it that way. Does that make sense?
During this time, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I wouldn’t say depressed most of the day nearly every day, no. I mean, I’ve been stressed and worn down by all of this, certainly, but “depressed” feels… maybe stronger than what I’d call it. I’m still getting through my days. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you had the feeling that someone can control your thoughts?
No… I don’t think so. I’ve never felt like someone was actually controlling my thoughts. I can get preoccupied with what’s going on, sure, but my thoughts still feel like mine. Is that what you mean?
Have you found yourself withdrawing from other people or losing interest in things you usually care about?

A little, yes… though I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I’ve just stopped functioning. I’ve pulled back from a few consulting jobs, and I’m not painting as much as I usually would. A lot of my week gets taken up following up with neighbors, offices, building staff—trying to get things sorted out. So I suppose I have withdrawn some, yes. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you believe there is a hidden system or conspiracy in the building specifically organized to force you out?

Well… “conspiracy” sounds a bit dramatic, and I don’t want to come across as unreasonable. But yes, I do think there’s a system to it. For months now, the property manager and certain people in the building have been… using things like misdelivered mail, noises in the walls at very specific times, little comments from neighbors—small things, but they line up too neatly.

It feels organized to pressure me out of the apartment. And I know they have paperwork and explanations for each piece of it, but those don’t really change the pattern I’m seeing. Does that make sense?
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so other people could know what you were thinking?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t had the sense that my thoughts are going out where people can hear them or know them. I mean, I do sometimes feel like people pick up on things or make comments that seem pointed, but not because they can hear my thoughts. My thoughts still feel private, if that’s what you’re asking.
Have you ever believed that an outside force was sending you special messages through the television, radio, or internet?

Not exactly through television or radio, no. I don’t want to overstate it. It’s more… in the building itself. The misdelivered mail, the noises in the walls that happen at particular times, and certain comments from neighbors—it feels like those are the messages, or signals, I suppose.

I know that may sound like I’m reading too much into things, but after months of it, the pattern is hard to ignore. Their paperwork and explanations don’t really account for how it all lines up. Is that answering what you mean?
If someone showed you clear proof that the property manager was not trying to force you out, would you be able to accept that?

I’d like to think I could, doctor. I mean, I don’t want to be stubborn or unfair to anyone.

But if I’m being honest… it would have to explain the whole pattern, not just one piece of it. Because they always have paperwork or explanations for the mail, or the noises, or what someone said, but that doesn’t really change how it all fits together. For months it’s felt like the property manager and certain people there are using those things to push me out.

So… clear proof might help, but I don’t know that I could just dismiss what I’ve been seeing. Does that sound unreasonable?
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that your thoughts seem jumbled?

No, not that I’m aware of. I mean, people have disagreed with me or said I’m focusing too much on certain things, but I don’t think anyone has said my speech is hard to follow or that my thoughts are jumbled.

I try to explain myself clearly. If I’m not doing that now, you’d tell me, right?
Before these problems in the building started, had you generally been a very suspicious person for most of your adult life?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve always tried to be careful and practical—my work sort of required that—but I wouldn’t say I was suspicious of people in general.

Maybe cautious, if that’s fair. But not the way things have felt with the building. Before all this started, I don’t think people would have described me as someone who was constantly suspicious. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed your emotions feeling noticeably flatter or less expressive than usual?

I don’t think so, no. At least, I haven’t noticed anything like that.

I may be tired or preoccupied at times, and maybe I don’t show things as much when I’m trying to stay composed, but I wouldn’t say my emotions feel flat. I still feel upset, concerned, relieved—normal things, I think.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Did this start very suddenly, within a couple of weeks?

No, not that suddenly. It’s been… closer to about 11 months now, I think—since not long after I moved into the new apartment.

I know that sounds like a long time when I say it out loud, but it didn’t feel like it all happened overnight. It sort of developed after I was there a little while. Does that answer what you mean?
Aside from dealing with the building situation, have you found it hard to motivate yourself to do everyday things?

Not generally, no. I mean, if I’m not caught up in dealing with the apartment situation, I can still take care of ordinary things.

I manage my finances, cook for myself, keep appointments—that sort of thing. And I can still talk in an organized way about consulting work or my painting. So I wouldn’t say I’ve lost motivation overall. It’s more that the building situation takes up a lot of my attention. Is that a fair way to put it?
Have you seen things that other people could not see?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t seen things that weren’t there, at least not that I’m aware of.

Sometimes I may notice something out of the corner of my eye and then it’s just a shadow or a reflection, but I assume that happens to people. Nothing like seeing a person or objects that other people can’t see. Is that what you mean?
For at least one month, have you held this belief that the property manager and neighbors are deliberately trying to force you out?

Yes… yes, for more than a month. I don’t want to sound unreasonable, but it’s been going on for months now.

It’s the pattern I can’t ignore—the misdelivered mail, noises in the walls that seem timed, and then little comments from certain neighbors. It feels like the property manager and some people in the building are trying to pressure me out of the apartment. They give explanations and paperwork, and I understand how that may look on paper, but it doesn’t really change what I’m seeing. Does that make sense?
Since this started, has your ability to work or manage your daily life become much worse than it was before?

Not much worse overall, I don’t think. I mean, it has taken up a lot of time and attention, but when I’m not dealing with the apartment situation, I can still manage the usual things.

I pay my bills, keep track of my finances, cook for myself, make my appointments. And if I’m talking about consulting work or my painting, I can still explain things in an organized way. So… I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I’ve fallen apart or anything. Is that answering it the way you mean?
Have you ever heard voices speaking to you or about you when no one else was there?

No, I don’t think I have. I mean, I’ve heard noises in the building, or people talking in the hallway sometimes, but not voices speaking to me when no one is there.

And I haven’t heard voices talking about me in an empty room or anything like that. If that’s what you mean, then no.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether overall work and daily functioning have become markedly worse since the belief started, which directly matches the profile item about functioning not being markedly impaired apart from the delusion’s impact.

patient.answer:
Not much worse overall, I don’t think. I mean, it has taken up a lot of time and attention, but when I’m not dealing with the apartment situation, I can still manage the usual things.

I pay my bills, keep track of my finances, cook for myself, make my appointments. And if I’m talking about consulting work or my painting, I can still explain things in an organized way. So… I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I’ve fallen apart or anything. Is that answering it the way you mean?

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are persistent auditory hallucinations, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever heard voices speaking to you or about you when no one else was there?

target_item.reason: The question asks about auditory hallucinations (hearing voices when no one is there), but the provided symptom profile covers delusions and functioning/duration, not hallucinations.

patient.answer:
No, I don’t think I have. I mean, I’ve heard noises in the building, or people talking in the hallway sometimes, but not voices speaking to me when no one is there.

And I haven’t heard voices talking about me in an empty room or anything like that. If that’s what you mean, then no.

inference.note: Persistent non-bizarre persecutory delusion for ~11 months with relatively preserved functioning and no hallucinations, thought disorder, negative symptoms, thought control/broadcasting, or marked deterioration makes F22 more likely and rules against F20.0.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview by understanding the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a fixed persecutory belief that the property manager and neighbors are deliberately trying to force them out, present for about 11 months and clearly for longer than 1 month. The belief is systematized and resistant to contrary explanations, while there are no clear hallucinations, thought broadcasting/insertion/control, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, prominent mood episode, or marked overall functional deterioration. This pattern is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder, persecutory type.
